label: first-token 3 / o-then-x at t=1, plus sparse early-copy firing
explanation: Sparse unit (0.9% of steps) with two regimes. (1) Original phase, almost entirely t=0 and t=1: it fires deterministically (precision 1.0) at t=0 when the input is 3, but weakly (bottom two activation quartiles, ~0.03 of max); at t=1 it fires in about 37% of cases when the previous token is o, plus scattered other t=1 pairs. (2) Copy phase, about 70% of activation mass, including all the strongest activations: early copy steps (recall_idx 1-4, mostly in long sequences with many outputs left, with the peak at t=10). The top examples are recall_idx 1 with copy inputs such as 2, s, b, q, but no token or position rule reaches more than ~8% precision there. Never fires at the delimiter, at recall_idx 0, or at original positions >= 3. The recorded predicate only covers regime (1): about 40% of activations and 22% of mass. The copy-phase component, which carries most of the mass, is unexplained.
